evidence.quote: are developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York state

summary.short: Adds Article 44-B (RAISE Act) to New York's General Business Law, requiring large developers of frontier AI models to implement and publish safety and security protocols, report safety incidents within 72 hours, and not deploy models posing unreasonable risk of critical harm. Effective 90 days after enactment.
summary.long: Adds Article 44-B, the Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act, to New York's General Business Law. The article applies to frontier AI models developed, deployed or operating in whole or in part in New York. A frontier model is defined by training computation exceeding a stated number of operations and compute cost above $100 million, or a distilled model with compute cost above $5 million. A large developer is a person that has trained at least one frontier model and spent over $100 million in compute costs in aggregate on frontier models. Before deploying a frontier model, a large developer must implement a written safety and security protocol, retain an unredacted copy, publish a redacted copy, record and retain test information, and implement safeguards against unreasonable risk of critical harm. It must not deploy a frontier model where doing so would create an unreasonable risk of critical harm. It must review the protocol annually, disclose safety incidents to the attorney general and the division of homeland security and emergency services within 72 hours, and not knowingly make false or materially misleading statements. The attorney general may bring a civil action for civil penalties of up to $10 million for a first violation and $30 million for a subsequent violation, or for injunctive or declaratory relief. The article creates no private right of action. The act takes effect on the ninetieth day after it becomes law.
